findings.text: Objectives tab lists each assessment objective with its methods; Record determinations judges every objective with its methods; the control takes the worst once all are judged.
Requests and determinations wait on the plan: D. Okafor approves, R. Calloway concurs, each recorded as its holder. A control added to an approved plan joins version 2.
Determinations read 'recorded as Nadia Fournier by Ingrid Solberg'; only the lead assessor publishes, recorded as D. Okafor, and the results and plan approvals say so.
One publish rule: every determination short of satisfied opens an operational issue, in continuous monitoring and in expanded set 2 alike (five issues there).
Result batches read 'Expanded set 1', 'Expanded set 2', 'set 1' on every page, dialog and toast; Increment names only acquisition increments.
A control names the campaign holding it from every campaign's requests and plans; AC-2(7) names the expanded campaign, offers Open assessment campaign, and Add refuses a second.
Assign owner (risks, issues, POA&M items), Deactivate, Change planned date and Link ATT&CK technique save; Overview, My work, People and the registers recount from them.
Create risk asks Mitigate, Accept or Transfer (Mitigate when a POA&M item answers it); an issue offers Create risk before its POA&M item; Mitigate drops Request acceptance.
Adversarial DT&E is proposed after the IATT (Jun 8); the recorded SA-24 exercise keeps its window but warns it starts before the IATT, which shows as a prerequisite lane.
Plan the test runs Plan an assessment's command: a campaign with a draft plan, on SSP 3 for Increment 2, listed on Assessments and Cyber T&E.
SVR's Cyber T&E deliverable names the CVI campaign's lead, Ingrid Solberg, as Cyber T&E and Assessments do.

extra.text: Plan an assessment offers SSP 3 (Increment 2) beside SSP 2, as lane G asked; the CVI defaults to SSP 3.
A campaign gains a Plan tab: each plan version, the controls it adds, and who approved or concurred, recorded as whom.
The Deactivated tab lists deactivated issues with reason and why, in place of 'Nothing is deactivated'.
